sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Ankit Agarval,Kamlesh Kumar Mishra,Kartikeya Saran,Vidya Kant T
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Chandan Sharma,G.A.
Hon'ble Shekhar Kumar Yadav,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA for the State and perused the record.
Learned counsel for the informant is also present.

2. This bail application under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure has been filed by the applicant seeking enlargement on bail during the trial in Case Crime No. 0090 of 2022, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 IPC, P.S. Jahangirpur, District Bulandshahr, during pendency of trial.

3. In short, as per prosecution story, the applicant in collusion with the co-accused persons is said to have got a sale deed executed in his favour belonging to the informant on the basis of a forged power of attorney, which is stated to be executed by one Mamta Devi and signed by the applicant as a signatory of the company.

Praveen Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68872201/
1 5.

sentences.text: Learned Counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant is an authorized person and has not acted individually rather he has acted on behalf of the company being the authorized signatory of the said sale deed.
The said amount has been transferred from the account of the company to the account of the said lady Mamta Devi through banking transactions.
No money has been exchanged in cash.

Learned counsel for the applicant has further stated that it is true that subsequent to it, the informant had filed a suit for cancellation of the sale deed and the said suit has been allowed ex-parte i.e. O.S. No.1085 of 2022 in addition to the other suits i.e. O.S. Nos.1082 of 2022 and 1083 of 2022.
Being ex-parte proceedings, the company of the applicant has challenged the said order and a restoration application is pending before the court concerned.
It is further submitted that the applicant is a bona fide person having no criminal antecedents to his credit and the dispute of civil nature has been converted into criminal one.
6. It is further submitted that the accused has not done anything illegal in the transaction of sale of the property related to the case.

The accused has neither sold the property related to the case in his personal capacity nor has he received the said property, moreover the accused has not received any consideration in exchange for the said property.
The accused was merely the authorized signatory of the company, which bought the property and then sold the property.
The accused is only the authorized signatory of the company and is not the beneficiary of the underlying transaction.
It is further submitted that no offence under sections 467, 468 and 471 IPC is made out against the accused and the offence under section 420 IPC is also not made out against the accused.
The FIR should have been lodged against the company or its directors.
It is further submitted that co-accused Mohit, Vinod, Liladhar, and Mamta Devi, have already been granted bail.
The applicant is in jail since 17.01.2024.

7. Learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for the informant have vehemently opposed this bail application on the ground that the applicant has committed forgery knowingly as the said Mamta Devi, the purported seller, is a domestic help to his house and was not in an economic condition to execute the said sale deed.
Even the applicant on behalf of the company has filed a suit for permanent injunction for being able to execute the sale deed of the remaining part of the land.

Learned counsel for the informant has further stated that the resolution dated 22.08.2019, by which the applicant has been made an authorized signatory, is forged one and there are two signatories in it i.e. Mahendra and Japesh Kumar.
On the date of the said resolution, only Japesh Kumar was a director and Mahendra was not a director in the company.
Learned counsel has further stated that an amount of Rs.59 lakhs has been usurped by the applicant by committing the said forgery.
The present case is not a case of civil nature.
It is true that the informant has incurred financial loss but the applicant has committed forgery, as such is not entitled for bail.

8. Perusal of record would disclose that the applicant is accused of having prepared a fake and forged power of attorney in the name of Mamta Devi (co-accused) working in his house from the Sub-Registration Office Doraha, District Tihar Madhya Pradesh on 22.02.2012 in connivance with other co-accused persons and got the deed of the said land registered in his favour from co-accused Mamta Devi, thereafter the applicant-accused sold the land to other co-accused persons, thus, it can be said that applicant is the kingpin in the present case, who is said to be accused of purchasing and selling of the agricultural land of the informant by preparing a fake and forged power of the Praveen Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/68872201/
2 attorney, hence the applicant/accused cannot be said to be a bonafide purchaser of the land in question.

sentences.text: 9. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, and looking to the nature and severity of allegations, without commenting on merits of the case, at this stage, this Court does not find it to be a fit case for grant of bail.
10. Accordingly, present application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. stands rejected and is consigned to record.
